newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed with risers and fallers.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed with risers and fallers.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Friday with gasoline falling, gas oil rising and naphtha and fuel steady.
Gasoline prices fell on a correction to this week's gains, lower values in NWE and adequate supplies of both premium unleaded and lower octane grades, traders said.
Premium unleaded cargoes fell $8 to $230/$232 cif.
"The Med is quite balanced to comfortably supplied," said one Italian trader, adding that this week some arbitrage opportunities opened to the U.S., Colombia and West Africa.
Naphtha was steady with cargoes at $222/$225.
The market was seen balanced but vulnerable to stronger NWE prices due to crude and swaps buying.
Gas oil prices rose, carried higher by Dec IPE futures which ended $1.50 higher at $220.75, and premiums were steady.

Traders reported active demand for heating oil was active, with a cargo loaded at Lavera sold for a reported cif quotes high +$1. A cargo of Russian was rumoured traded at cif quotes high +$5. Traders cited another other parcel at high quotes +$4.50 fob Italy.
Demand for low sulphur diesel was moribund with lower quotes receiving little buying interest.

High and low sulphur cracked fuel was steady on Friday with little interest heard. The Mediterranean remains stronger than the north because supplies of Russian straight-run are more scarce than in NWE. Good demand for bunker material also kept prices around $110-112 fob Med.
Low sulphur cracked fuel was slow with the main Med buyer standing back after recent price hikes that have added up to $10 a tonne since last week. The sector looks balanced to tight.
Black Sea Russian fuel exports were noticeably thinning which has kept premiums steady. M-40s in particular were lacking. -- London newsroom, +44 171 542 7646
